prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-20. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.30 |
| Retained earnings       | 33,239M |
| Current liabilities     | 13,326M |
| Current assets          | 17,271M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 29,093M |
| Total liabilities       | 43,439M |
| Total assets            | 73,680M |
| EBIT / operating income | 1,498M |
| Revenue                 | 34,015M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-20, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company's financial health appears concerning. While the current ratio of 1.30 is acceptable, the significant debt burden indicated by Total Liabilities (43,439M) being substantially higher than Shareholders' Equity (29,093M) points to high leverage. Furthermore, EBIT (1,498M) relative to Revenue (34,015M) suggests thin operating margins, which may strain its ability to service this debt.

DECISION: BB
